nodes.label: lexicon build README
nodes.rationale: Levels are annotated onto a big dictionary corpus rather than sourced from an open CEFR list, because the app's own placeholder word 'ubiquitous' is absent from every open CEFR-graded list.

nodes.label: Lexicon build pipeline (WikDict + CEFR-J + Octanove + wordfreq)
nodes.rationale: Python is used here on purpose in a TypeScript repo because wordfreq (the frequency/inclusion-filter source) is Python-only, and the script is offline, one-off, and touches nothing the app's own infrastructure owns.

nodes.label: pnpm level:lexicon Batches-API CEFR leveling job
nodes.rationale: Only ~15% of the corpus has a human CEFR level; an --eval pass on 300 human-graded rows showed Haiku collapses at the hard end (C2 recall 5/25) while Opus 5 scored higher there, and since the unlevelled tail is mostly hard dictionary words, Opus 5 was chosen despite costing ~4x more.
